# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54 (Bi-Vb Pc54)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc54
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating more after refusing an offer
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc54
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54 (Bi-Vb Pc54), titled *Pavārita* ("Eating more after refusing an offer"), stipulates that a Buddhist nun who consumes food after having finished her meal and refused further offerings commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The origin narrative (*vorgeschichte*) of this rule is completely identical to the initial version of the corresponding rule for monks, Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 35 [Hüsken 1997]. While the origin story employs the phrasing *bhuttāvī pavāritā* ("having eaten and having refused"), the rule itself uses *nimantitā vā pavāritā vā* [Hüsken 1997]. The casuistry of both rules corresponds for the most part, though the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*) in the nun's rule shares only one specific exemption with the monk's rule—namely the permissible consumption of afternoon tonics or medicines (*yāmakālika*, *sattāhakālika*, *yāvajīvika*) when there is a requisite cause (*sati paccaye*) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the rule in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Dharmaguptaka (Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 148), Sarvāstivāda (Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 157), and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan (such as xct-mu-bi-vb-pc141) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reflect this close relationship: the text shares its largest Pali-internal overlap with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 35 (over 3,600 characters matching at 0.93 similarity across §0.4–1.19), closely aligning with Hüsken's textual comparison [DharmaNexus; Hüsken 1997]. DharmaNexus also notes extensive formulaic sharing with other Vinaya dining and disciplinary rules (such as Bu-Vb Pd 1, Bu-Vb Pd 3, and Parivāra 1.2), alongside cross-language alignments with Tibetan canonical works including the *Bhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtra* (D0004), the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120), and the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* [DharmaNexus].
